pl-l2d35c3-d1e108.summary: Reports some who, attending to Augustine's words, teach learnedly that evil will and acts are good insofar as they are or are acts, a good nature of God and from him; insofar as done inordinately, against the law, and lacking due end, they are sin, and as sin are nothing, no substance or nature.
claims: Acts are good as acts and sinful as inordinate.

pl-l2d35c3-d1e111.summary: Reports their proof from Augustine's Quaestiones: God is cause only of good, so not author of evil, since he is author of all that is, and all that is is good insofar as it is.
claims: Whatever is, is good.

pl-l2d35c3-d1e114.summary: Cites Augustine proving nothing happens by chance: what happens by chance is not by providence; if something were by chance, some nature would be outside providence; but all that is is good insofar as it is, by participation in the highest good, called divine providence; so nothing happens by chance.
claims: Nothing happens by chance.
All things are good by participation in the highest good.

pl-l2d35c3-d1e120.summary: States that they rely on these to show all that is, insofar as it is, is good.

pl-l2d35c3-d1e123.summary: Cites De doctrina christiana I: he is supremely and first who is wholly immutable; other things can only be from him and are good insofar as they have received being.
claims: Things are good insofar as they are.

pl-l2d35c3-d1e126.summary: Infers that evil will and action, since they exist, are good insofar as they are, and as will or action; they are evil by vice, which is not from God and is nothing.
claims: Evil acts are good as being and evil by vice.

pl-l2d35c3-d1e129.summary: Cites the 83 Questions: the vice of the will by which man is worse is far from God's will, as reason teaches.
claims: Vice is not from God's will.

pl-l2d35c3-d1e132.summary: Reports they prove from this that will, insofar as vicious, is not from God and is sin, lacking due order and end; likewise action insofar as it proceeds from evil, lacks order, and tends to evil.
claims: Sin lacks due order and end.

pl-l2d35c3-d1e135.summary: Reports another proof: no act would be evil unless it were a good thing, since nothing is evil unless the same thing is good.
claims: An evil thing is a good thing.

pl-l2d35c3-d1e139.summary: Cites the Enchiridion: every nature is good; nothing would be evil unless the evil thing were a nature; so evil cannot be unless something is good; absurd as it sounds, reasoning compels us to say it.
claims: Evil presupposes good.

pl-l2d35c3-d1e144.summary: Reports their conclusion: all acts, insofar as they are, are good things; nothing is evil, that is sin, unless it is also good in some respect; God is author of all that is insofar as it is, and all things are by his will, being natures insofar as they are.
claims: God authors all things insofar as they are.

pl-l2d35c3-d1e147.summary: Raises the objection: then adultery, homicide, and the like, insofar as they are, are good, natures, and willed by God, and those who do them do good, which is absurd.

pl-l2d35c3-d1e150.summary: Reports their reply: adultery and homicide denote not simply acts but acts with their vices; the acts, insofar as they are acts, are from God and good natures, but not insofar as they are adultery and homicide; so it does not follow that adultery and homicide are from God.
claims: Acts are from God, not their vices.

pl-l2d35c3-d1e153.summary: Raises another objection: if nothing is evil that is not a good nature, how are not believing in God or not going to church sins, since these are not natures or anything at all?

pl-l2d35c3-d1e156.summary: Reports their reply: such expressions, though negative, really posit acts: not believing in Christ is unbelief, an evil act of mind; not going to church signifies contempt, an evil will or intention, a turning from good; as turning from evil posits a will to avoid evil, turning from good posits a will to evil. So Augustine's general definition of mortal sin holds.
claims: Omissions signify acts of the will.

pl-l2d35c3-d1e162.summary: Raises a further question for them: since sin is privation or corruption of good and every evil act is sin, is it so insofar as sin? If so, since privation of good is a punishment, sin as sin would be punishment, and so good and from God; if not, it would be a privation insofar as good.

pl-l2d35c3-d1e165.summary: Reports their answer: the evil act is privation of good not insofar as it is or is good, but insofar as it is sin; yet not punishment or from God, since sin is called privation actively, not passively: it deprives a good nature of some good and harms it, and it harms only insofar as it is sin.
claims: Sin is privation actively, not passively.

pl-l2d35c3.summary: Reports the learned view that evil will and acts are good insofar as they are, or are acts, and from God, but sin insofar as they are inordinate, against the law, and lacking due end; as sin they are nothing, no substance or nature. They cite Augustine that God causes only good, all that is is good insofar as it is, nothing happens by chance, and the vice of the will by which man is worse is far from God's will. To the objection that adultery and homicide would then be good and willed by God, they reply that these names signify acts with their vices; the acts as acts are from God, not as adultery or homicide. To the objection that omissions like not believing or not going to church are no things, they reply that such negations signify acts, unbelief or contempt, an evil will. Asked whether sin as sin is privation of good and so punishment and from God, they answer that sin is privation actively, not passively: it deprives nature of good and harms it insofar as it is sin.
claims: Some hold that evil will and acts are good insofar as they are acts and from God.
On that view, acts are sins insofar as they are inordinate, against the law, and lacking due end.
As sin, an act is nothing, neither substance nor nature.
Everything that is, insofar as it is, is good, and nothing happens by chance.
Adultery and homicide name acts with their vices; the acts as acts are from God.
Sins of omission signify acts of the will, such as unbelief or contempt.
Sin is privation of good actively, not passively.
